---
title: "ANSI-escaped stream output keeps single newlines"
format: html
engine: jupyter
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      ensureHtmlElements:
        -
          - "div.cell-output-stdout div.ansi-escaped-output pre span.ansi-red-fg"
          - "div.cell-output-stderr div.ansi-escaped-output pre span.ansi-red-fg"
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        -
          - 'line one(\r\n?|\n)<span class="ansi-red-fg">line two</span>(\r\n?|\n)line three'
          - '<span class="ansi-red-fg">first write</span>second write'
          - '<span class="ansi-red-fg">stderr one</span>(\r\n?|\n)stderr two'
        -
          - 'line one(\r\n?|\n){2}'   # blank line after the first line
          - 'line two</span>(\r\n?|\n){2}'   # blank line after the colored line
          - 'first write</span>(\r\n?|\n)second write'   # newline inserted between two writes
          - 'stderr one</span>(\r\n?|\n){2}'   # blank line in stderr
---

Stdout containing ANSI escape codes is converted to HTML spans inside `div.ansi-escaped-output`. In the notebook, stream `text` is stored as a list of lines that each keep their trailing newline, so the lines must be concatenated as-is. Joining them with an extra newline shows a blank line between every output line (#13966).

```{python}
print("line one\n\033[31mline two\033[0m\nline three")
```

Consecutive writes to the same stream are merged into one output, so a write without a trailing newline must stay on the same line as the next one.

```{python}
import sys
print("\033[31mfirst write\033[0m", end="")
sys.stdout.flush()
print("second write")
```

The same applies to stderr.

```{python}
import sys
print("\033[31mstderr one\033[0m\nstderr two", file=sys.stderr)
```
